body.statement: For every \(h_0\in(0,\infty)\), the absolute \(\Lambda\)-mass of the propensity-path component is \(\int |h_0u/(1+h_0s)^2|\,d\Lambda=\alpha\operatorname{Beta}(1+\kappa,1-\kappa)E_H|u|\,h_0^{-\kappa}\). Hence this component is absent at a finite critical coordinate if and only if \(u=0\) \(H\)-almost surely; if \(E_H|u|>0\), it remains strictly positive for every finite \(h_0\) and vanishes only at the stable endpoint \(h_0\to\infty\). Moreover \(\int|g_{h_0}(s,r,u)-r/s|\,d\Lambda=O(h_0^{-\kappa})\).
body.justification: This prevents invalid residual-only critical calibration and identifies precisely when the extra causal-policy mark can be ignored.
body.gap: Neither Kennedy2019Incremental nor the scalar boundary laws in MaWang2020RobustIPW characterize equality of these marked Lévy pushforwards.
body.consumer: Software can use the criterion to decide whether a simpler stable-mark approximation is legitimate at a finite hardening coordinate.
